cards.claim: In non-uniform circular motion the total acceleration is the vector sum of the centripetal and tangential accelerations.

cards.claim: The centripetal and tangential accelerations are perpendicular: one is radial, the other tangential.
cards.quote: Note that the two acceleration vectors a → c a → c and a → T a → T are perpendicular to each other, with a → c a → c in the radial direction and a → T a → T in the tangential direction.

cards.claim: The net acceleration in circular motion points to the centre only when the speed is constant; with changing speed it has a tangential part too.
cards.quote: The resultant acceleration of an object in circular motion is towards the centre only if the speed is constant.
